items.speaker: Female Storekeeper
items.text: Have a good day!
Before the owner can even say goodbye, Liáng has yanked Poitier out the front door.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: What's the rush? I haven't even finished my noodles.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: We can eat later, but we need to find Ms. Latham, now!

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Wait, wait. Hold on. I'm all for chasing down a crook. But why do I get the feeling you didn't tell your Foundation friend about your run-in with Latham?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: What's up? Why you keeping her in the dark?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I think that something isn't right about her.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I've been to the ACD before. To most, it might seem defenseless, but it's actually heavily protected by arcane rituals.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: According to Ms. Scott, Latham acted alone.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: But there's nothing in her file that would suggest she's capable of that. Her arcane skill level is frankly far from remarkable.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Even with insider knowledge, I don't believe it's possible she could have bypassed the security system and escaped on her own.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Either Ms. Latham has playing the Foundation for fools, or she has more powerful accomplices. That leads me to another thing. This mission is not something a typical Foundation staff member would be assigned to—as Ms. Scott claimed to be.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: There's something we don't know.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: You're saying that girl with glasses lied to you?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Maybe, or that she was being lied to herself.
Liáng pulls her SPF-I contact device from beneath her cloak. After a few simple taps, she turns it around for Poitier to see.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: There was another thing I found while searching through Ms. Latham's files, or rather, what I didn't find—there were no warnings or notices on her employee records.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: You mean, she's not actually wanted?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: No, I don't think so.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Ms. Scott said that their department wanted to solve this problem in secret, so I thought that might explain the reason Ms. Latham's warrant wasn't on her file.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: However, when I tried to access more of their records to double-check my findings, I ran into a block on Ms. Scott's records.

items.speaker: Notification
items.text: Access denied. You do not have permission to view this information. If you need access, please contact your supervisor.
A warning symbol flashes on the screen.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: It could just be because I'm only a cadet. There are some files that I don't have access to yet. I contacted my supervisor, but I haven't heard anything back.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I don't mean to distrust her, but I can't hold anyone above suspicion.
Poitier shifts her gaze from the device's screen back to Liáng.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: And what about me? You're putting a lot of trust in me, Liáng. Is it really alright that you're telling me all this?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: A dangerous item stolen from the Foundation and possibly an inside job at that. That's a scandal in the making.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: You could've just lied to me, make up some kind of story. It's not hard for a smart kid like you.
Liáng gives Poitier a puzzled look.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Why would I? We're partners, Ms. Poitier. Hiding information from you wouldn't be right. You told me that yourself, didn't you?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Me?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Yes, the first day we were on duty together, you said you "need to know what makes me tick."

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Hmm, I did, didn't I?
Poitier seems a little dazed. Liáng looks at her, sincerity behind her eyes.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I've reconsidered it, and you're right.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: During my training as a vigil, our instructor emphasized many times that trusting in our partner was of vital importance.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: And you, Ms. Poitier, have proven to be capable, decisive, and compassionate. I have developed a deep respect for your work.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: We share the same goal: to discover the truth behind the incidents happening in Chinatown. I can't think of any reason why I shouldn't cooperate with you.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Alright, alright, alright. Enough. I'm blushing already.
Poitier cuts Liáng off, almost flustered.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Damn, girl! I didn't expect my meek little mouse to turn into this.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: This what?

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Forget it. You've made your point. Now, stop it.
Poitier waves a hand, signaling the conversation's end.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: But you kinda missed my point. I'm worrying that the Foundation is gonna punish you for leaking classified information. Won't you get in trouble?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Though I may be a vigil of the Foundation, before that, I am a descendant of the Liáng family. I'm obliged to do all that is necessary to fulfill my destiny.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: And given the circumstances, I think providing all relevant information that might assist us in catching the thief and retrieving these threatening arcane objects is worth bending the rules ... just a little.
Despite her conviction, Liáng can't help but hesitate a little.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Besides, I'm not under any orders to keep this a secret. So ...

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Haha. Cheeky, and you say you don't like bending the rules. I see you, boo.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: And I like it. Come on. Let's work this out together, partner.
Hotel Room

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Which one is my room again? Oh, right, I wrote it down. Let me see. There it is. I almost went too far again.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Now, the key card. Where did I put it—oh, here.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Home, sweet home. Oh, I'm exhaust—
The camera-headed girl freezes in place.
Two officers are standing in her sweet home.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: Latham, right? It's been a while.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: We have some questions for you. Please try to cooperate.
Liáng steps forward and closes the door on her behalf.
When an unsuspecting prey steps into a carefully laid trap, the outcome is already decided.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Alright. Fine. I'll tell you everything.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: It was me, okay? They said I stole those arcane objects and sold them for money, well, maybe I did—Ouch!
As she speaks, she backs closer and closer to the wall behind her, until she smacks her oversized head into the window ledge.
A particular word in her statement makes Liáng tilt her head.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: What do you mean "maybe"?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Because, actually, I can't remember it.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: I can't find my memory film for that time, so really, I just don't know.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Memory film?
This so-called Loggerhead girl, an Awakened, isn't exactly a tough one. Within thirty minutes, she has spilled everything.
Yet, despite this seemingly ideal result, neither of the officers looks pleased.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: *sigh* So, to summarize what you just said, Latham:

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: You're an Awakened piece of a movie projector, which forms a Latham loop.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: You were designed to play movies, not record them, and that's why you suffer from severe amnesia.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: You can only recall things that happened within the last three days, and after that, you'll forget almost everything, do I got that right?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: I guess so.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: You guess so?

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Eek!
Poitier's sudden questioning startles the girl. She shrinks further into the corner, wedging herself between the window and a nearby chair.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: I can see why that friend of yours calls you Loggerhead. You deserve the name. What is going on here?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: It's understandable. Awakened arcanists often suffer side effects related to their origins and materials, but still, this is quite unusual, to say the least.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: So, she has no memory of what happened three days ago, or even any of the cases she was involved in. So then, she's basically useless to our investigation.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I can only imagine what a disaster it would be if you showed up in a Detective C07 movie.

items.speaker: Loggerhead
items.text: Hey! That's rude! How come I'm a disaster?
The girl, mustering what little courage she has left, waves her metal fists in defiance.
But her feeble resistance has no effect on the officers. After sighing in unison, they exchange a glance.

items.speaker: Poitier
items.text: What do you think?

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: I've made a request for Ms. Latham's detailed records. But, I don't think she's lying.

items.speaker: Liang Yue
items.text: Back at the hospital, the best lie she could come up with was "a hamster riding a stethoscope." I kind of doubt she's a master manipulator.
